claims.text: Closed-loop real-time thermal control during laser deposition will reduce rapid local temperature fluctuations and thermal gradients.
Reducing rapid thermal gradients will mitigate residual-stress formation.
Mitigating residual stress will reduce fabrication-induced defects.
Closed-loop thermal control will improve dimensional precision relative to fixed laser parameters.
Closed-loop thermal control will improve mechanical integrity relative to fixed laser parameters.
Additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components can exhibit defects associated with temperature gradients and internal stress.
The relevant fabrication defects specifically include porosity and microcracks.
Uncontrolled rapid thermal gradients cause dimensional inaccuracies in additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components.
The proposed control system dynamically adjusts laser power and scan speed from real-time temperature-sensor feedback.
The intervention is intended for high-entropy alloys processed under powder-blown laser directed-energy-deposition conditions.
The intervention will produce more uniform cooling rates in each deposited layer.
Real-time adjustment of energy input modulates melt-pool dynamics and cooling rates.
A more stable thermal environment reduces porosity and microcrack formation.
Reducing porosity and microcracks leads to more accurate layer deposition.
Reducing porosity, microcracks, and residual stress improves the integrity of the final mechanical structure.
Fixed-parameter additive manufacturing produces pronounced thermal gradients and associated defects.
The benefits of closed-loop control may diminish when ambient fluctuations or sensor and actuator delays prevent effective real-time control.
The magnitude of dimensional and mechanical improvement may vary with sensor responsiveness, integration challenges, and alloy thermal properties.
